transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-10-20
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Chris (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Alex (NexaHealth CTO), Priya (ML), Ben (Infra), Samira (Product)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): Weekly POC sync - cover onboarding progress, environment readiness, share benchmark results, discuss tuning KV cache and batching, agree next steps.

00:00 Alex Romero: Hey everyone, uh, thanks for doing the weekly, I know we're tight on time so I'll just flag the infra blockers up front.
00:09 Chris Patel: Yep thanks Alex, we can go quick. Maya on deck to walk the benchmarks and then we'll hit the VPC/IAM checklist.
00:16 Maya Lin: Cool. Quick note - I pulled the last run from Friday; ran the 2k request workload with a 512 token avg, there were, um, a couple spikes in tail latency. I'll share the spreadsheet after this call.
00:31 Priya Singh: When you say spikes, are we looking at GPU queueing or network? Last time it felt like we had KV cache misses.
00:38 Maya Lin: Good call, Priya. The profiler shows a high KV cache miss rate for longer prefixes - which increases decoder cost. We suggested increasing prefix caching for your chat flows and to batch slightly higher for throughput windows.
00:54 Ben Carter: Quick status - VPC peering is in progress, I created the peering but we still need to accept from the account side and then set up route tables. I also need the cross-account role ARN from Redwood.
01:04 Chris Patel: ARN is in the onboarding doc - link in the email, but I'll paste again. It's redwood-prod-role-73482, I'll DM the exact ARN after this.
01:12 Alex Romero: Great. On IAM, we want minimal privileges - ok to do read-only S3 and assumed role?
01:19 Maya Lin: Yes read-only for the dataset is fine; we need write for logs to the Red-collection bucket if you want Redwood to ship debug logs back, otherwise read-only is OK.
01:30 Samira Ochoa: On data residency — just to reiterate, pilot data must stay in our AWS account, no long-term retention on vendor side. What's Redwood's default retention for POC traces?
01:41 Chris Patel: For hosted POC runs we keep ephemeral traces for 14 days by default and those can be configured; for Dedicated or Private we can align with your retention matrix. We'll attach the retention SLA doc and the network diagram.
01:51 Priya Singh: Ok thanks. Back to the benchmark, can you walk through the single-request latency distribution and the cost per 1K tokens?
02:00 Maya Lin: Sure - so median token latency was about 18 ms per token, p95 about 120 ms in the noisy runs. Cost - the spreadsheet has two columns; with default batching we saw $0.012 per 1K tokens, with aggressive batching we dropped to about $0.007 per 1K, but tail latency worsened. We can tune batching windowing to hit your SLOs.
02:26 Alex Romero: Hmm that delta seems reasonable. Our product SLO for chat is p95 under 300 ms so sounds ok. We need to ensure p99 is decent on 10K concurrent users though.
02:40 Maya Lin: For p99 under high conc we recommend a hybrid approach: dedicated baseline plus burst on hosted, or increase dedicated pool size. For the POC we'll run an experiment next week simulating 10K concurrent small requests to see how KV cache hit rate holds up.
02:58 Ben Carter: That test will blow up our NAT gateway unless we route through the peered network; let's ensure the peering is finished before the spike.
03:06 Chris Patel: Agreed — action item for Ben to finish peering. We'll keep the test to non-working hours if needed.
03:12 Priya Singh: On tuning - you mentioned prefixing keys for KV cache. Do you have a config sample?
03:18 Maya Lin: Yes, sample config - basically key the cache on conversation_id + last N tokens, set cache TTL to 30s for active sessions, increase cache size for embeddings reuse. I'll attach the sample config; quick note: you might need to bump instance memory if you grow cache size.
03:33 Priya Singh: Memory is fine, but we need to confirm our dedicated instance type. Are you recommending A10G or H100X for the pilot?
03:41 Maya Lin: For latency-focused chat H100X gives best raw perf, but quantized L4/FP16 on A10G is cost-efficient. For the pilot we suggested A10G dedicated pool with smart routing; if you need guaranteed sub-200ms p95 at production scale we'd move to an H100 class.
03:58 Alex Romero: Cost tradeoff noted. For now stay A10Gs - we have budget limits.
04:03 Samira Ochoa: Security asks — can we get a short SOC2 summary and the network diagram? Our security team asked specifically about KMS integration and audit logs.
04:12 Chris Patel: Yes, we'll attach SOC2 and ISO summaries, and KMS integration notes. We support customer-managed KMS for Private/Dedicated. Audit logs are available in the Redwood Console; we'll share the export link.
04:24 Priya Singh: One more thing - the model variants: for some flows we want a lower-cost embedding-first rerank stage. Can Redwood support a hybrid pipeline?
04:33 Maya Lin: Absolutely, you can route to an embedding model for candidate generation then to a lightweight generation model for final assembly. We have built-in reranking and model chaining - we'll share a reference architecture doc.
04:44 Ben Carter: Back to infra: are there specific subnet requirements? Our VPC is in us-east-1, private subnets only, NAT via TGW.
04:53 Maya Lin: Works fine. We just need outbound access to the Redwood control-plane endpoints for orchestration; if you want completely private we can jump to Private deployment, but that needs a longer lead time. For this POC outbound to specific IP ranges is enough.
05:07 Priya Singh: Ok we're good on region. Regarding the sample dataset - I will upload to s3://nexa-poc/samples but need the bucket policy example.
05:17 Chris Patel: I'll paste the bucket policy template in the follow-up email.
05:22 Alex Romero: Great. Are there any blockers from Redwood side for the next benchmark run?
05:27 Maya Lin: No blockers, just we need the S3 link, peering accepted, and the assumed role ARN. Once we have those three items we can schedule the 10K spike test.
05:36 Priya Singh: I'll try to get the S3 link today. Ben will work on peering.
05:40 Ben Carter: Yep will accept and push route entries by tomorrow EOD.
05:45 Chris Patel: Perfect. Quick recap and next steps—we'll run the big benchmark Tue 2027-10-26 if infra is ready; Maya to lead benchmark run, Chris to share spreadsheet and SOC2 docs, Priya to upload dataset.
05:58 Alex Romero: Sounds good. Anything else?
06:01 Samira Ochoa: Just one ask - can you include a short template of success criteria for pilot acceptance, so we can align internally?
06:08 Chris Patel: Yep I'll include a one-pager success criteria template.
06:12 Alex Romero: Awesome, thanks everyone.
06:15 Chris Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email and put action items into the CRM.
06:19 (call ends)
